general_purpose.policy: The minimum practical good starting tier for an average PC or laptop is a capable 7B-9B instruction model at a quality-preserving 4-bit-or-better quantization, 8 GiB dedicated VRAM where available, 16 GiB system or unified memory, and at least 8k tested context. Treat this as a pilot floor, not a guarantee.

hard_rejections.reason: 512M/1B/2B-class models are specialist or experimental routes, not general-purpose defaults.
Below-4-bit weights are outside the general-purpose quality floor.
Q1-class quantization is rejected for 27B-and-larger routes; use a smaller capable model at Q4-or-better or add memory.

hard_rejections.when: required tools or structured output have not passed the route trial
hard_rejections.reason: Text generation alone does not prove agent, tool-call, schema or cancellation compatibility.

hard_rejections.when: runtime estimate plus 15% headroom exceeds available memory
hard_rejections.reason: Do not route by weight-file size alone; context/KV cache and runtime allocations also consume memory.

not_for: silent replacement of a stronger required route

evidence_limit: Runtime documentation supports hardware variability, memory estimation/offload controls, and the context-memory relationship. Tier thresholds and exclusions are conservative repository recommendations requiring a task-specific trial, not vendor benchmarks or universal quality claims.
